notes.front: What is a Certificate of Aircraft Registration for a small unmanned aircraft, in one sentence?
notes.back: The FAA document showing a small unmanned aircraft is registered; registration takes effect on its date of issue.
notes.explanation: Part 107 flying needs an effective registration, done online under part 48 or, like manned aircraft, under part 47.
notes.example: An owner registers a drone online on FAADroneZone, pays the fee and receives a Certificate of Aircraft Registration for it.
notes.source: 14 CFR §§ 48.25(a), 48.100(b) (eCFR); FAA Advisory Circular 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (2021), ¶5.4
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 48 as of that date

notes.front: What is the unique identifier on a registered small unmanned aircraft?
notes.back: The registration number issued by the FAA (or, if the FAA authorises, the aircraft's serial number) displayed on the aircraft.
notes.explanation: It links the aircraft in the air to its registration, so it must be displayed before the aircraft is flown.
notes.example: A label printed with the FAA registration number, stuck to the outside of the drone's body.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 48 as of that date

notes.front: When must a small unmanned aircraft be registered to fly under part 107?
notes.back: Before it is operated: under part 48 (online) or part 47.
notes.explanation: § 107.13 applies § 91.203(a)(2), which requires an effective registration certificate for the aircraft.
notes.source: FAA Advisory Circular 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (2021), ¶5.4; 14 CFR §§ 107.13, 91.203(a)(2)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · AC 107-2A (2021), current on that date

notes.front: Which small unmanned aircraft are exempt from registration because of their weight?
notes.back: Only those flown exclusively under 44809 recreational rules and weighing 0.55 lb or less on takeoff.
notes.explanation: Aircraft of the U.S. Armed Forces are also exempt. A part 107 aircraft must be registered whatever it weighs.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 48 as of that date

notes.front: A 0.5 lb drone will film a paid real-estate shoot under part 107. Must it be registered?
notes.back: Yes. The 0.55 lb exemption covers only aircraft flown exclusively under 44809 recreational rules.
notes.choices:
A) No: it is under 0.55 lb
B) Yes: the weight exemption is only for 44809 recreational flying
C) Only if it flies over people
notes.choicesExplained: A: the weight exemption applies only to aircraft flown exclusively under 44809. C: registration does not depend on flying over people.
notes.explanation: Easy to confuse: Category 1 for flying over people also uses 0.55 lb, but that does not affect registration.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 48 as of that date

notes.front: A 0.4 lb drone is flown purely for fun, keeping to all the 44809 rules. Must it be registered?
notes.back: No: an aircraft flown exclusively under 44809 and weighing 0.55 lb or less is exempt.
notes.explanation: If the owner later uses it for a part 107 job, it must be registered first.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 48 as of that date

notes.front: You buy a new drone on Monday for a part 107 job on Wednesday. What must be done before its first flight?
notes.back: Register it (online under part 48, or part 47) and mark it: under part 48, display its unique identifier on an external surface.
notes.explanation: An aircraft is registered only once the owner receives its Certificate of Aircraft Registration.
notes.source: FAA Advisory Circular 107-2A, Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (2021), ¶5.4; 14 CFR §§ 48.100(b), 48.200 (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · AC 107-2A (2021), current on that date

notes.front: A Certificate of Aircraft Registration expires {{c1::3 years}} after its date of issue unless renewed.
notes.explanation: A renewed certificate runs for three years from the previous certificate's expiry date.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 48 as of that date

notes.front: A part 107 drone's registration was issued on 10 May 2023 and never renewed. May it fly a job on 12 May 2026?
notes.back: No: the registration expired on 10 May 2026, 3 years after issue. Renew it first.
notes.explanation: Renewal can be done any time in the six months before the month of expiry.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 48 as of that date

notes.front: When may you renew a Certificate of Aircraft Registration?
notes.back: Any time within the six months before the month in which it expires.
notes.explanation: Renewal means verifying, and if needed updating, the registration information.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 48 as of that date

notes.front: Issuing or renewing registration for a part 107 small unmanned aircraft costs {{c1::$5.00}} per aircraft.
notes.explanation: The fee is paid through the web-based registration system. A 44809 recreational certificate also costs $5.00, but per certificate.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 48 as of that date

notes.front: Who must register a small unmanned aircraft owned by a 12-year-old?
notes.back: A person at least 13 years old.
notes.explanation: Otherwise the owner registers the aircraft in their own legal name.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 48 as of that date

notes.front: Registration details must be updated online within {{c1::14 calendar days}} of a change, or of a sale, destruction or export.
notes.explanation: The holder must keep the registration information accurate at all times.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 48.115 Requirement to maintain current information (eCFR)
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 48 as of that date

notes.front: You sell your registered part 107 drone to a friend. What must you do, and by when?
notes.back: Update the online registration to cancel it, within 14 calendar days of the sale.
notes.explanation: Sale or transfer, destruction and export all require cancellation through the registration system.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 48 as of that date

notes.front: You move house. What must you do about your drone's registration?
notes.back: Update the address in the online registration system within 14 calendar days.
notes.explanation: Any change to the information given on the application must be updated within 14 calendar days.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 48 as of that date

notes.front: Where must the unique identifier be displayed?
notes.back: Legibly, on an external surface of the small unmanned aircraft.
notes.explanation: It must also be kept in a legible condition.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 48 as of that date

notes.front: How must the unique identifier be attached to the aircraft?
notes.back: By any means that keeps it affixed for the whole of each operation.
notes.explanation: The rule does not prescribe a method, only the result.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 48 as of that date

notes.front: Your registration number is written only inside the drone's battery compartment. Does that meet the marking rule?
notes.back: No: it must be legibly displayed on an external surface.
notes.explanation: An identifier hidden inside the aircraft cannot be read from outside it.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 48 as of that date

notes.front: You tape a paper label with the registration number to the outside of your drone, but it tends to fall off during flights. Compliant?
notes.back: No: the identifier must stay affixed for the duration of each operation, and stay legible.
notes.explanation: Any method is allowed, as long as it lasts the flight and remains readable.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 48 as of that date

notes.front: Can a small unmanned aircraft owned by a lawful permanent resident of the United States be registered under part 48?
notes.back: Yes, provided it is not registered in another country.
notes.explanation: U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, certain U.S.-based corporations and U.S. governments may register.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 48 as of that date

notes.front: Is registration evidence of who owns a small unmanned aircraft?
notes.back: No. Registration is not evidence of ownership in a dispute over who owns it.
notes.explanation: The rule follows 49 U.S.C. 44103(c).
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 48 as of that date

notes.front: How does registration differ for a part 107 drone and for drones flown only under 44809?
notes.back: Part 107: one certificate per aircraft. 44809-only: one certificate covers all the owner's recreational aircraft.
notes.explanation: Both certificates last 3 years; the part 107 fee is per aircraft, the 44809 fee per certificate.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 48 as of that date

notes.front: Registration and Category 1 both mention 0.55 lb. What does 0.55 lb exempt a part 107 drone from?
notes.back: Not from registration. For part 107, 0.55 lb matters only for Category 1 over people.
notes.explanation: The registration exemption at 0.55 lb applies only to aircraft flown exclusively under 44809.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-25 · 14 CFR Part 48 as of that date
